critique.evidence: The screen supports an operational defense story with PR-AUC, constrained-FPR recall, calibration, latency, confusion counts, value caught/blocked, and an ablation showing Provenance materially affects PR-AUC. However, the visible evidence never connects these measurements to intent integrity or Mastercard-specific payment authorization outcomes. Dataset size, attack mix, decision thresholds, benchmark protocol, and provenance of the reported results are absent; “results artifact” is only a label. The precision-recall chart’s repeated 100% tick labels also weakens interpretability, while every ablation reports 100% fresh-row recall despite materially different PR-AUC.
critique.fix: Tie each metric to the protected payment intent and Mastercard use case: show approved intent versus manipulated execution, attack cohorts, operating thresholds, sample sizes/confidence intervals, and benchmark provenance. Add an explicit end-to-end comparison demonstrating that the defense prevents unauthorized intent changes while preserving legitimate transactions, and correct the PR chart labels.
